title: Required App Never Settled — ESP Completion Deferred
description: The IME reported its user-session completion line, but at least one required app stayed pending — without ever failing or even starting to install — so the agent kept deferring the enrollment completion signal. Typically an assignment/requirement problem (requirement rules never met, dependency never satisfied, or the app needs a context that is not available during ESP, e.g. a VPN client waiting for user sign-in to a portal).
author: Autopilot Monitor

preconditions.description: Suppress when the pending app eventually settled and the enrollment completed — a transient deferral is normal.
Suppress when the session failed explicitly — the app/ESP failure rules already cover that path; this rule targets the never-finishing case.

explanation:
The Intune Management Extension wrote its user-session completion line, but the agent observed `{{pending}}` required app(s) still pending (`{{pendingNames}}`) and therefore **deferred the enrollment completion signal** — repeatedly, if this happened across several logons or reboots.

A pending app that never transitions to downloading/installing and never fails is almost always an **assignment or requirement problem**, not an install error:

- requirement rules that are never met on this device (OS/architecture/registry/script checks),
- an unsatisfied dependency or supersedence chain,
- an app targeted as *required* for the user ESP that needs something unavailable during provisioning (e.g. a VPN client whose portal sign-in only happens after first logon),
- user-targeted apps on a device where the user identity never fully registered (see the hybrid user-affinity rule if it also fired).

remediation.title: Identify and unblock the pending app
steps: Check the app names listed in this finding's evidence (pendingNames) — these are the apps the ESP is waiting for.
In Intune, review the app's requirement rules and dependencies; test them on the device (IntuneManagementExtension.log logs each requirement evaluation).
Decide whether the app really must block the ESP: removing it from the ESP's 'blocking apps' list (or making it not-required during enrollment) unblocks completion immediately.
If the app is user-targeted on a hybrid-joined device, verify the user's Entra affinity first — without a signed-in Entra user, user-targeted policy never applies.
